calls.reasoning: Status quo: the AA leaderboard (v5.0.1) shows Gemini 4 Carbon (high) at 60 and Claude Opus 5.5 (max) at 59, so with no change the question resolves at 60. Reference class: when a new frontier model took the lead within the same index version, the top score usually rose 1-4 points. In v3/v4 that worked out to about 2 pts/month, which implies roughly +3 over the 53 days left. Trackers project several frontier releases before Dec 31 (GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.1 Astra, Grok 4.8, Claude Fable 5.5, Claude Opus 5.6), but none has a confirmed date. Releases late in December may not be benchmarked by Dec 31. v5's heavy weight on private test sets may slow gains. I put about 30% on no new leader by Dec 31 and a small chance that rescoring moves the top down to 59. Markets: Manifold 'any model 60+ by Nov 20' trades at 0.86 on 151 volume. That contract has a different deadline and threshold, and the displayed 60 already effectively satisfies it, so it is not an anchor. I found no market on the Dec 31 maximum.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs report the same leaderboard snapshot (top 60, v5.0.1) and the same tracker-projected releases, so the factual base is consistent. The 59-vs-60 discrepancy (Oct 31 background and a Nov 4 third-party snapshot vs 60 on Nov 8) is probably the v5.0.1 CritPt rescoring of Nov 3 or rounding near the boundary. I can't fully settle it without web access, so I keep about 8% of mass at 59 or below. Run 3's historical rates come from memory, not fetched data, but they match Run 2's account of v4 (top rose to 66 over Jan-Oct), so I accept roughly 2 pts/month as the reference rate. The remaining disagreement is judgment: how many projected releases ship and get benchmarked before Dec 31, and how big their gains are. The runs agree on about 30% no-change; I agree and see no evidence to move it. I put the median near 61, just above the status-quo mass, and give a moderate right tail for a strong Opus 5.6, Fable 5.5 or GPT release. Neither bound looks plausible to escape, so I price no mass outside the range.
